text: In any triangle,  (if) one of the sides (is) produced  (then) the external angle is equal to the (sum of the) two internal and opposite (angles), and the (sum of the) three internal angles of the triangle is equal to two right-angles. Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let one of its sides $BC$ have been produced to $D$. I say that the external angle $ACD$ is equal to the (sum of the) two internal and opposite angles $CAB$ and $ABC$, and the (sum of the) three internal angles of the triangle---$ABC$, $BCA$, and $CAB$---is equal to two right-angles.
For let $CE$ have been drawn through point $C$ parallel to the straight-line $AB$ [Prop.~1.31].
And since $AB$ is parallel to $CE$, and $AC$ has fallen across them, the alternate angles $BAC$ and $ACE$ are equal to one another [Prop.~1.29].
assertion: alternate angles BAC and ACE are equal to one another

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: alternate angles $BAC$ and $ACE$ are equal to one another

text: Again, since $AB$ is parallel to $CE$, and the straight-line $BD$ has fallen across them,  the external angle $ECD$ is equal to the internal and opposite (angle) $ABC$ [Prop.~1.29].
assertion: external angle ECD equals the internal and opposite angle ABC

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the straight-line $BD$ has fallen across them

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: external angle $ECD$ is equal to the internal and opposite (angle) $ABC$

text: But $ACE$ was also shown (to be) equal to $BAC$.
assertion: angle ACE was shown equal to angle BAC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $ACE$ was also shown (to be) equal to $BAC$

text: Thus, the whole angle $ACD$ is equal to the (sum of the) two internal and opposite (angles) $BAC$ and $ABC$.
assertion: whole angle ACD equals the sum of the two internal and opposite angles BAC and ABC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: whole angle $ACD$ is equal to the (sum of the) two internal and opposite (angles) $BAC$ and $ABC$

text: Let $ACB$ have been added to both.
assertion: add angle ACB to both sides

text: Thus, (the sum of) $ACD$ and $ACB$ is equal to the (sum of the) three (angles) $ABC$, $BCA$, and $CAB$.
assertion: ACD plus ACB equals the sum of the three angles ABC, BCA, and CAB

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (the sum of) $ACD$ and $ACB$ is equal to the (sum of the) three (angles) $ABC$, $BCA$, and $CAB$

text: But, (the sum of) $ACD$ and $ACB$ is equal to two right-angles [Prop.~1.13].
assertion: ACD plus ACB equals two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (the sum of) $ACD$ and $ACB$ is equal to two right-angles

text: Thus, (the sum of) $ACB$, $CBA$, and $CAB$ is also equal to two right-angles.
assertion: ACB plus CBA plus CAB equals two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (the sum of) $ACB$, $CBA$, and $CAB$ is also equal to two right-angles

text: Thus, in any triangle,  (if) one of the sides  (is) produced (then) the external angle is equal to the (sum of the) two internal and opposite (angles), and the (sum of the) three internal angles of the triangle is equal to two right-angles. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
